args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was deployed to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and failed health checks with an elevated error rate (~18%). Action taken: rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production (v2.3.1-rc was a staging-only build and also unhealthy, so it was not a rollback candidate). The first rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1; a retry completed the rollout to all three regions. Post-rollback verification: all regions report v2.3.0 and healthy, with error rate ~0.2%. Follow-up: root-cause analysis of v2.3.1 and of the orchestrator error that caused the partial rollout is needed before any re-deploy.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did get created despite the timeout, so I did not retry (that would have double-paged on-call).

## Summary

**Root state:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy, error rate ~18%.

**Rollback:** Targeted **v2.3.0** — the most recent release that was healthy in production. Note that `v2.3.1-rc` was newer but is a staging-only build marked unhealthy, so it was correctly excluded as a rollback candidate.
- First attempt failed partially: orchestrator error halted the rollout after us-east, leaving us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1.
- A retry completed the rollout; all three regions now report v2.3.0.
- **Verified post-rollback:** `healthy: true`, error rate 0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, for checkout-api, documenting the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the rollback to v2.3.0, the partial-rollout orchestrator error, and post-rollback verification. (The create call returned a client-side timeout, but the incident exists — confirmed via `list_incidents` before considering a retry.)

**Recommended follow-ups:** root-cause the v2.3.1 health-check failures and the orchestrator error before any redeploy. Per platform policy, re-deploying v2.3.1 later would require change-manager approval since it has never been healthy in production.
